changelog: - **e2e: a rate-limit flood no longer spends everybody else's bucket** (#2159). `enforceRateLimit` keys on `bucket:ip` into a per-process store, and a full-suite shard runs its whole file list against one Next server (`workers: 1`, one `webServer`) — so every request that arrives without a usable address counts into the same `<bucket>:unknown` counter. `rate-limit.spec.ts`'s six POSTs to `/api/support` (limit 5, 15-minute window) therefore left `support-attachments.spec.ts` and `support-chat.spec.ts` with nothing to spend, and shard 4/4 of `e2e-full` was red on the same two tests on every non-skipped scheduled run rather than intermittently. The new `e2e/helpers/rateLimit.ts` hands out synthetic `X-Real-IP` addresses — `floodIp()` a stable one for a test that is *measuring* the brake and must spend one counter repeatedly, `freshIp()` a new one per call for a spec that merely has to drive a rate-limited endpoint to reach the feature behind it. It goes through `x-real-ip` rather than `X-Forwarded-For` precisely because the webServer runs with `TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT=0` so the #858 spoofing test can prove a rotating forwarded header buys nothing — that test keeps the address it did not choose, since sharing is its whole claim. `support-chat.spec.ts` alone posts seven support messages against a limit of five, so a per-spec budget would only have moved the cliff; the browser-driven sends are covered too (`extraHTTPHeaders` on the context, `page.setExtraHTTPHeaders` on the default fixture), and `admin-support.spec.ts`, flagged in the report as the next exposure, is isolated in the same pass. No product code changes: the limiter is unchanged and still asserted.
